title: Expose content-bound section pairing over persisted ingest runs
body:
## Why

The existing section-pairing library has no supported persisted-run command and replayable comparison artifact.

Both reviewers substantively accepted a narrower replacement. The original mixed PDF section pairing with the different DOCX-by-ID journey.

Reviewed evidence at `6591255c3b32b2d2a7ff010a417358689640f873`:

src/doc_lineage/blackline.py:62-190 supplies section trees, alignment and NDJSON pairing decisions; src/doc_lineage/mutations/detect.py:30-38 is the only production-code caller found by direct source search. src/doc_lineage/cli.py:20-96 has no comparison command. tests/blackline/test_section_id_pairing.py:257-307 already proves ingest-to-pairing composition using substituted Docling output, including persisted segment assertions, but does not reload two independent persisted runs through a production command. The DOCX exporter consumes original DOCX packages rather than PDF-derived pairing edges.

Current source readback: `src/doc_lineage/blackline.py:62` at `b9daca70b27f452d62d8c6ccdb3bcd3b5dc7a783` (file SHA-256 `c339f553462d1437ee512e07ef5a20a401779dedf703c904534b3003f907afd7`). Earlier detailed line ranges and reproductions retain their reviewed-commit provenance; intervening anchor changes were checked for relevance.

## Scope

Provide a local command/API that loads and validates two existing ingest runs, calls the existing section-tree and pairing functions, and publishes a versioned, content-bound comparison artifact with an opaque lookup ID. Bind ordered source hashes, segment-artifact hashes and pairing options, and document replay behavior. Coordinate a compatible local comparison identity envelope with Codex candidate 4 while keeping native DOCX lookup/export acceptance in that separate candidate.

## Non-Goals

- Do not implement PDF-to-DOCX conversion or claim PDF section-pair artifacts complete DOCX export by ID.
- Do not implement the native DOCX lookup/export journey owned by Codex candidate 4 in this candidate.
- Do not implement HTML rendering, new semantic alignment heuristics, or infer confirmed supersession from section alignment.
- Do not change shared fleet contracts or require a hosted service; define repo-owned comparison details using existing run/identity conventions.
- Use the revised section-pairing scope, sharing only the identity envelope with F09. No PDF-to-DOCX conversion or claim that F09 is complete.
- Scaffold-only or partial completion does not count as done: deliver the specific Scope behavior and Acceptance Criteria evidence, rather than only a helper, an unconnected call path or an empty passing test run.

## Tasks

- [ ] Define the local comparison identity envelope binding ordered source digests, segment artifact digests and pairing options; coordinate compatibility with the separately approved DOCX lookup scope; target `src/doc_lineage/blackline.py`.
- [ ] Add a supported CLI/API consumer for two existing ingest-run directories and validate source/manifests before calling the existing section tree and alignment functions.
- [ ] Persist the section-pairing artifact under an opaque comparison ID and implement fresh-invocation lookup with explicit unknown-ID, tamper and source-order failures; target `src/doc_lineage/blackline.py`.
- [ ] Exercise two distinct synthetic PDF versions across independent ingest/comparison/replay invocations and document the boundary from native DOCX export and semantic supersession.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] An integration test ingests two synthetic PDFs with genuinely different original-byte hashes, starts a separate comparison invocation using only their persisted run directories, and checks ordered source hashes, validated segment-artifact hashes and emitted section-pair decisions against the existing pairing engine.
- [ ] A fresh invocation resolves the opaque comparison ID and reopens the same persisted artifact; reversing the source order or changing pairing-relevant inputs cannot silently resolve to the prior comparison.
- [ ] Unknown IDs, a path passed as an ID, missing artifacts and segment payloads that no longer match their manifest fail clearly before publishing a comparison artifact.
- [ ] Existing unmatched, duplicate-ID and low-confidence manual-review behavior survives. Documentation labels this as section pairing, distinguishes it from classified text differences and native DOCX tracked changes, and leaves README issue-15 completion pending until the separate DOCX replay acceptance passes.
- [ ] Run `python -m pytest tests/blackline/test_section_id_pairing.py -q` with nonzero collection and the named scope-specific behavior assertions passing; retain the actual command/result in the delivery evidence.
- [ ] Deliberate-break gate: after adding the scope-specific regression in `tests/blackline/test_section_id_pairing.py`, temporarily disconnect its corresponding Scope change at `src/doc_lineage/blackline.py`; that regression must fail on the described behavior. Restore the change and rerun it successfully, capturing both outcomes.
